docs.title: Database Infrastructure Documentation
docs.text:
Welcome to the technical documentation for the Database Infrastructure.

This documentation covers the processes and procedures for deployment, configuration, monitoring, backup, recovery, automation, and troubleshooting of database and infrastructure services.

docs.title: Documentation Goals
docs.text:
The goal of this project is to provide a centralized knowledge base for documenting configurations, architectures, daily operational procedures, automation, and troubleshooting solutions.

This documentation is continuously maintained and updated based on real-world operational experience and infrastructure requirements.

docs.title: Project Setup Guide
docs.text:
This guide explains how to set up, update, preview, and contribute to the documentation project on Linux and Windows systems.

The project uses:

  • Git
  • Python
  • Python Virtual Environment
  • MkDocs
  • Material for MkDocs
  • GitHub

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before setting up the project, make sure the following tools are installed:

Tool Purpose Git Version control and synchronization with GitHub Python 3 Running MkDocs pip Installing Python packages venv Isolating Python dependencies MkDocs Material Building and serving the documentation

docs.title: Ubuntu / Debian
docs.text:
sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y git

Verify the installation:

git --version

Example:

git version 2.x.x

docs.title: 2.2 Install Python
docs.text:
Check whether Python is already installed:

python3 --version

If Python is not installed:

sudo apt update
sudo apt install -y python3 python3-pip python3-venv

Verify:

python3 --version
pip3 --version

docs.title: 3.1 Install Git
docs.text:
Download and install Git for Windows from the official Git website.

After installation, open PowerShell or Git Bash and verify:

git --version

docs.title: 3.2 Install Python
docs.text:
Install Python 3 from the official Python website.

During installation, make sure to enable:

Add Python to PATH

Verify the installation:

python --version

and:

pip --version

docs.title: 4. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
Clone the documentation repository from GitHub.

Using SSH:

git clone git@github.com:mohammadsafyar/docs.git

Or using HTTPS:

git clone https://github.com/mohammadsafyar/docs.git

Move into the project directory:

cd docs

Verify the repository:

git status

Expected output:

On branch main
Your branch is up to date with 'origin/main'.

docs.title: 5. Create a Python Virtual Environment
docs.text: Using a virtual environment keeps the project's Python dependencies isolated from the system Python installation.

docs.title: Linux
docs.text:
python3 -m venv venv

Activate the environment:

source venv/bin/activate

You should see something similar to:

(venv) user@server:~/docs$

docs.title: Windows PowerShell
docs.text:
Create the environment:

python -m venv venv

Activate it:

.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

If PowerShell blocks script execution, run:

Set-ExecutionPolicy -ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned -Scope CurrentUser

Then activate again:

.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

docs.title: Windows CMD
docs.text:
Create the environment:

python -m venv venv

Activate:

venv\Scripts\activate

docs.title: 6. Install Project Dependencies
docs.text:
After activating the virtual environment, upgrade pip:

python -m pip install --upgrade pip

Install the project dependencies:

pip install -r requirements.txt

If requirements.txt does not exist yet, install Material for MkDocs directly:

pip install mkdocs-material

Verify MkDocs:

mkdocs --version

docs.title: 7. Project Structure
docs.text:
The project should have a structure similar to:

docs/
├── .github/
│   └── workflows/
│       └── ci.yml
│
├── docs/
│   ├── index.md
│   │
│   ├── sql-server/
│   │   └── backup.md
│   │
│   ├── postgresql/
│   │   └── index.md
│   │
│   ├── linux/
│   │   └── index.md
│   │
│   └── ansible/
│       └── index.md
│
├── mkdocs.yml
├── requirements.txt
├── README.md
└── .gitignore

The docs/ directory inside the repository contains the Markdown documentation files.

docs.title: 8. Local Preview
docs.text:
Before pushing changes to GitHub, always test the documentation locally.

Make sure the virtual environment is active:

source venv/bin/activate

On Windows:

.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

Start the MkDocs development server:

mkdocs serve

By default, MkDocs runs on:

http://127.0.0.1:8000/

Open the address in your browser.

docs.title: 8.1 Use Another Port
docs.text:
If port 8000 is already in use, run:

mkdocs serve -a 127.0.0.1:8001

Then open:

http://127.0.0.1:8001/

docs.title: 9. Build the Documentation
docs.text:
Before committing changes, it is recommended to verify that MkDocs can build the entire documentation successfully.

Run:

mkdocs build --strict

A successful build should finish without errors or warnings.

The generated website will be created in:

site/

The site/ directory is a generated build artifact and should normally not be committed to Git.

docs.title: 10. Updating the Documentation
docs.text:
Before starting new work, always synchronize your local repository with GitHub.

Make sure you are inside the repository:

cd docs

Then:

git pull origin main

This downloads the latest changes from GitHub.

docs.title: 11. Creating or Editing Documentation
docs.text:
Documentation files are written using Markdown.

For example:

docs/sql-server/backup.md

Edit the file using your preferred editor:

nano docs/sql-server/backup.md

or:

vim docs/sql-server/backup.md

After making changes, preview them locally:

mkdocs serve

docs.title: 12. Adding a New Documentation Section
docs.text:
When adding a new section such as PostgreSQL, Linux, or Ansible, create the required directory and Markdown file.

Example:

mkdir -p docs/postgresql
touch docs/postgresql/index.md

Then add the section to mkdocs.yml:

nav:
  - Home: index.md

  - SQL Server:
      - Backup: sql-server/backup.md

  - PostgreSQL:
      - Overview: postgresql/index.md

The referenced Markdown file must exist.

For example:

docs/postgresql/index.md

docs.title: 13. Check Git Changes
docs.text:
After modifying the documentation, check the repository status:

git status

Review the changes:

git diff

For new files, use:

git status

to verify that the expected files are detected.

docs.title: 14. Commit Changes
docs.text:
Add the required files:

git add .

Review what will be committed:

git status

Create a commit:

git commit -m "Update documentation"

Use descriptive commit messages whenever possible.

Examples:

git commit -m "Add PostgreSQL documentation"

git commit -m "Update SQL Server backup guide"

git commit -m "Add Linux administration section"

docs.title: 15. Push Changes to GitHub
docs.text:
Push the changes to the main branch:

git push origin main

After a successful push, the changes are available in the GitHub repository.

If GitHub Pages is configured for automatic deployment, the published documentation will be updated automatically.

docs.title: 16. Recommended Daily Workflow
docs.text:
Use the following workflow whenever you work on the documentation:

1. Pull latest changes
       ↓
2. Edit Markdown / mkdocs.yml
       ↓
3. Run MkDocs locally
       ↓
4. Review the documentation
       ↓
5. Run mkdocs build --strict
       ↓
6. git status
       ↓
7. git add
       ↓
8. git commit
       ↓
9. git push

Commands:

git pull origin main

# Edit documentation

mkdocs serve

mkdocs build --strict

git status
git add .
git commit -m "Update documentation"
git push origin main

docs.title: 17. Working from Multiple Systems
docs.text:
GitHub is the central source of truth for this project.

For example:

              GitHub
                 │
        ┌────────┴────────┐
        ↓                 ↓
     Linux             Windows
        │                 │
     git pull          git pull
        │                 │
      Edit              Edit
        │                 │
     git push          git push
        └────────┬────────┘
                 ↓
              GitHub

docs.title: Important Rule
docs.text:
Always run:

git pull origin main

before starting work on a different system.

This helps ensure that you are working with the latest version of the documentation.

docs.title: Port 8000 Already in Use
docs.text:
Error:

OSError: [Errno 98] Address already in use

Use another port:

mkdocs serve -a 127.0.0.1:8001

docs.title: MkDocs Cannot Find a Page
docs.text:
Example:

WARNING - A reference to 'postgresql/index.md'
is included in the 'nav' configuration,
which is not found in the documentation files.

Verify that the referenced file exists:

docs/postgresql/index.md

Also verify the path in mkdocs.yml.

docs.title: Git Says There Is Nothing to Commit
docs.text:
If:

git status

returns:

nothing to commit, working tree clean

but you expected changes, check:

git diff

and:

git ls-files

Also verify that you are working inside the correct repository:

pwd
git remote -v

docs.title: Push Is Rejected
docs.text:
If Git reports:

rejected
non-fast-forward

do not immediately use git push --force.

First synchronize with GitHub:

git pull --rebase origin main

If a conflict occurs, resolve the conflict before continuing the rebase.

docs.title: 19. Virtual Environment Management
docs.text:
The virtual environment does not need to be committed to Git.

The venv/ directory should be included in .gitignore:

venv/

To deactivate the virtual environment:

deactivate

To activate it again:

docs.title: Linux
docs.text: source venv/bin/activate

docs.title: Windows PowerShell
docs.text: .\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

docs.title: 20. Quick Setup
docs.text:
For a new Linux or Windows system, the basic setup is:

git clone git@github.com:mohammadsafyar/docs.git
cd docs

python3 -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate

pip install -r requirements.txt

mkdocs serve

For Windows PowerShell:

git clone git@github.com:mohammadsafyar/docs.git
cd docs

python -m venv venv
.\venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1

pip install -r requirements.txt

mkdocs serve

The documentation should then be available at:

http://127.0.0.1:8000/

docs.title: 21. Summary
docs.text:
The project follows a simple workflow:

Clone
  ↓
Create Virtual Environment
  ↓
Install Dependencies
  ↓
Pull Latest Changes
  ↓
Edit Documentation
  ↓
Preview with MkDocs
  ↓
Build with --strict
  ↓
Commit
  ↓
Push

The most important commands are:

git pull origin main
mkdocs serve
mkdocs build --strict
git status
git add .
git commit -m "Update documentation"
git push origin main

Keep the GitHub repository as the single source of truth and always synchronize before working from another system.

docs.title: مقدمه
docs.text: Backup یکی از مهم‌ترین بخش‌های نگهداری SQL Server است و باید به‌صورت منظم اجرا و به‌صورت دوره‌ای Restore آن تست شود.

docs.title: Full Backup
docs.text:
نمونه دستور برای گرفتن Full Backup:

BACKUP DATABASE [MyDatabase]
TO DISK = 'D:\SQLBackups\MyDatabase_FULL.bak'
WITH
    COMPRESSION,
    CHECKSUM,
    STATS = 10;

docs.title: بررسی Backup
docs.text:
برای بررسی Backupهای ثبت‌شده در SQL Server می‌توان از Query زیر استفاده کرد:

SELECT
    database_name,
    backup_start_date,
    backup_finish_date,
    type,
    backup_size
FROM msdb.dbo.backupset
ORDER BY backup_finish_date DESC;

docs.title: نکات مهم
docs.text:
• Backup باید طبق یک Schedule مشخص اجرا شود.
  • فایل Backup باید روی Storage مناسب نگهداری شود.
  • Backupها باید از نظر موفقیت بررسی شوند.
  • Restore تستی باید به‌صورت دوره‌ای انجام شود.
  • نگهداری Backup باید مطابق سیاست Retention سازمان باشد.
